knowledge:
- key_parameters: wavelet=The wavelet function to use, typically "mexh" (Mexican Hat) ;; scales=A vector of scales (e.g., seq(1, 64, 2)) where smaller scales target narrow peaks/noise estimation and larger scales target wider peaks ;; winSize=The window size used for local maximum detection ;; MassSpecWavelet.localMaximum.algorithm=Global option ("classic", "faster", or "new") controlling the local maximum search behavior ;; SNR.Th=Signal-to-Noise Ratio threshold for peak identification ;; nearbyPeak=Logical flag indicating whether to include nearby peaks in the identification process
- alternatives: Traditional peak detection algorithms that rely on aggressive baseline correction and smoothing preprocessing steps, which are highly sensitive to parameter tuning and can be inconsistent across runs.
- when_to_use: When processing low-resolution mass spectra (such as SELDI and MALDI data) or other spectral profiles where high noise levels and baseline shifts make traditional amplitude-based peak detection unreliable.
- pitfalls: The "classic" local maximum algorithm uses non-sliding overlapping windows and can miss peaks (especially on plateaus or small window sizes); the "new" algorithm is experimental and may detect more maxima, potentially altering downstream pipeline results. Additionally, using excessively large scales can merge adjacent narrow peaks.

workflows.name: cwt_peak_detection
workflows.intent: Detect, identify, and refine peak parameters in mass spectrometry intensity profiles using Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) and ridge-line tracking.
input: exampleMS (numeric vector representing raw mass spectrometry intensity values across m/z indices)
workflows.stages: 1. Perform Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) using the Mexican Hat wavelet ;; 2. Identify local maxima of CWT coefficients across scales ;; 3. Connect local maxima into ridge lines ;; 4. Identify major peaks based on SNR thresholds ;; 5. Refine peak parameter estimations (center, width, strength)
workflows.code:
data(exampleMS)
scales <- seq(1, 64, 2)
wCoefs <- cwt(exampleMS, scales = scales, wavelet = "mexh")
wCoefs <- cbind(as.vector(exampleMS), wCoefs)
colnames(wCoefs) <- c(0, scales)
localMax <- getLocalMaximumCWT(wCoefs)
ridgeList <- getRidge(localMax)
SNR.Th <- 3
nearbyPeak <- TRUE
majorPeakInfo <- identifyMajorPeaks(
  exampleMS,
  ridgeList,
  wCoefs,
  SNR.Th = SNR.Th,
  nearbyPeak=nearbyPeak
)
betterPeakInfo <- tuneInPeakInfo(exampleMS, majorPeakInfo)

workflows.name: one_step_peak_detection
workflows.intent: Run the entire CWT-based peak detection and parameter refinement pipeline in a single encapsulated step.
input: exampleMS (numeric vector representing raw mass spectrometry intensity values across m/z indices)
workflows.stages: 1. Run the encapsulated peak detection pipeline ;; 2. Extract major peak information ;; 3. Refine peak parameter estimations (center, width, strength)
workflows.code:
data(exampleMS)
SNR.Th <- 3
nearbyPeak <- TRUE
peakInfo <- peakDetectionCWT(exampleMS, SNR.Th=SNR.Th, nearbyPeak=nearbyPeak)
majorPeakInfo = peakInfo$majorPeakInfo
betterPeakInfo <- tuneInPeakInfo(exampleMS, majorPeakInfo)
